name: SAM.gov
purpose: Find contract opportunities, entity registrations, and exclusion records in the official federal system.
limitations: A registration or notice is not proof of capability, past performance, or accessibility. Some records require sign-in or government access.
method: Search the public opportunity and entity pages, then record the notice or entity identifier, date, and what you actually searched.
use_when: Use when you need current federal opportunities, entity registrations, or exclusions.
questions: Are there current or recent notices for this product or service? Is the entity registered? Is there an exclusion record?
authentication: Public search; some records or actions may require sign-in or government access.
record_how: Record the notice or entity identifier, URL, search date, filters, and whether you found a notice, registration, or exclusion.
search_strategy: Search the official public pages by product/service terms, NAICS or PSC, agency, and date range. A registration is not proof of capability or accessibility.

name: Acquisition.gov
purpose: Read the current FAR, agency supplements, and acquisition policy text.
limitations: Policy text does not decide applicability or create a legal determination; agency deviations and effective dates still need verification.
method: Record the part, section, effective date, and any deviation you checked.
use_when: Use when you need the current FAR, agency supplement, or acquisition policy text.
questions: What does the current policy say? Which part or section applies? Is there a deviation or effective date?
record_how: Record the part and section, URL, as-of date, and whether the text is proposed, final, or a deviation.
search_strategy: Search the FAR part/section or agency supplement. Verify currentness and any deviation before relying on it.

name: USAspending.gov
purpose: Find comparable federal awards, recipients, agencies, amounts, and periods of performance.
limitations: A past award does not establish current fitness, availability, price, or accessibility. Data lags and scope vary.
method: Use the award search and record the award identifier, filters, date, and limitations.
use_when: Use when comparable awards or recipient and agency spending patterns are relevant.
questions: What awards were made for similar work? Who received them? What were the amount, agency, and period of performance?
record_how: Record the award identifier, recipient, amount, agency, period, filters, retrieval date, source-as-of date, and limitations.
search_strategy: Search award keywords, NAICS or PSC, agency, and fiscal year. A past award does not establish current fitness or availability.

name: eCFR
purpose: Read the operative electronic Code of Federal Regulations text as of a chosen date.
limitations: The eCFR is not a legal determination; verify currentness and agency-specific guidance.
method: Record the title, part, section, and as-of date.
use_when: Use when the operative regulation text and its date matter.
questions: What does the regulation say as of a date? Has it changed?
record_how: Record the title, part, section, as-of date, URL, and how you checked currentness.
search_strategy: Search the title, part, or section. Compare with current agency guidance before treating it as applicable.

name: Section508.gov
purpose: Use GSA's official Section 508 acquisition, ACR, and accessibility guidance.
limitations: Guidance does not determine conformance or approve an exception for a specific product.
method: Follow the applicable acquisition or ACR guidance and record the page and date.
use_when: Use for official Section 508 acquisition, ACR, and accessibility guidance.
questions: What accessibility requirements apply? How do I request and review an ACR? What is the exception process?
record_how: Record the page and date, the requirement or ACR guidance used, and any agency-specific step. Do not record general guidance as product conformance.
search_strategy: Start with buy/sell and ART guidance for requirements, then ACR and exception guidance. Use an accessibility specialist for applicability.

name: GSA Accessibility Requirements Tool (ART)
purpose: Generate tailored Section 508 requirements for an ICT purchase or development effort.
limitations: An ART output identifies requirements, not product conformance or an approved exception.
method: Follow official guidance and retain the requirements generated for the specific acquisition.
use_when: Use to generate acquisition-specific Section 508 requirements.
questions: Which requirements apply to this ICT? What functionality must be evaluated?
authentication: Public tool; an agency process may require an account or specialist.
record_how: Record the ART output, version or date, and requirement identifiers. ART produces requirements, not a conformance result.
search_strategy: Use the official ART flow for this acquisition and save the generated requirements with the research record.

name: GSA ACR Editor
purpose: Create or work with machine-readable OpenACR reports.
limitations: An ACR is a report of claims and findings, not an independent procurement approval.
method: Request version-matched ACRs from suppliers and verify claims by additional evaluation.
use_when: Use to draft or review an ACR against a catalog.
questions: How are criteria reported? Which criteria are missing or not evaluated?
authentication: Public; some workflows may require an account.
record_how: Record the product, version, catalog, date, and that the ACR is a draft or supplier claim.
search_strategy: Select the applicable catalog and review every criterion. Do not treat a completed ACR as an independent test.

name: Section508.gov: Buy or Sell Accessible ICT
purpose: Understand accessibility requirements and acquisition responsibilities.
limitations: Agency-specific procedures and current rules must also be reviewed.
method: Use the buyer guidance alongside your agency Section 508 program.
use_when: Use for the Section 508 buy/sell process guidance.
questions: What steps apply to this ICT acquisition? What documentation is expected?
record_how: Record the guidance page and date, then confirm the agency-specific process.
search_strategy: Read the buy/sell guidance before requesting an ACR or planning an exception question.

name: Section 508 ICT exceptions guidance
purpose: Identify whether any narrow exception might warrant formal review.
limitations: Do not treat a possible exception as an authorized determination.
method: Preserve required evidence and send it through agency approval procedures.
use_when: Use to identify the exception process and the questions an authorized official must answer.
questions: Is an exception category potentially relevant? Who is authorized to decide?
record_how: Record the guidance and route the question to the authorized official. Do not record a determination.
search_strategy: Read the exceptions guidance and document the question, evidence, and owner. This tool cannot approve an exception.

name: FY 2025 Section 508 assessment recommendations
purpose: Identify program improvements related to acquisition, oversight, and exceptions.
limitations: Recommendations are not a standalone product evaluation standard.
method: Use as context when designing quality checks and follow-up responsibilities.
use_when: Use for Section 508 program assessment context and expectations.
questions: What assessment expectations apply to the agency or program?
record_how: Record the page and date and note the relevance to the agency process.
search_strategy: Read the current assessment guidance; do not infer product conformance from a program assessment.

name: GSA ACR Issue Detail Supplement
purpose: Request additional details on barriers, severity, and impact.
limitations: Supplemental claims still need verification.
method: Ask suppliers to provide issue-level details for partial support or failures.
use_when: Use for issue-detail supplement fields and supplier follow-up questions.
questions: What detail should an ACR include for a criterion? What should we ask the supplier?
record_how: Record the supplement and date and use it to draft a question, not to fill in missing supplier evidence.
search_strategy: Read the supplement fields and ask the supplier for product-specific evidence.

name: GSA OpenACR
purpose: Machine-readable ACR schema and tools.
limitations: This starter does not yet parse or validate OpenACR YAML, PDF, DOCX, or HTML files.
method: Record ACR URLs and metadata now; add upstream OpenACR validation in the next phase.
use_when: Use for the machine-readable ACR format and validation.
questions: How is an ACR structured? Are required fields present?
record_how: Record the repository or tool version, imported file, and validation result. An import is not certification.
search_strategy: Use the upstream docs and local import; preserve the original ACR file and its source URL.

name: SAM.gov via 1102tools
purpose: Research notices, registered entities, certifications, and exclusions.
limitations: Hosted and local editions differ in coverage and freshness; registration is not proof of delivery capability.
method: Use the existing MCP through an AI host; record exact records, retrieval dates, and source dates.
use_when: Optional: use only when an approved MCP client connects the 1102tools SAM server.
questions: Same questions as SAM.gov, retrieved by an upstream tool.
authentication: Requires an approved MCP host and whatever SAM access the upstream tool requires.
record_how: Record the upstream tool, version, query, retrieval time, and URL. This project does not call it automatically.
search_strategy: Use only in an approved environment. Record provenance and do not treat a tool response as independent verification.

name: USAspending via 1102tools
purpose: Research comparable contracts, agency purchases, and incumbent suppliers.
limitations: Past contracts do not imply current capability or market completeness.
method: Search comparables, inspect award scopes, and retain record links.
use_when: Optional: use only when an approved MCP client connects the 1102tools USAspending server.
questions: Same questions as USAspending.gov, retrieved by an upstream tool.
authentication: Requires an approved MCP host and network access.
record_how: Record the upstream tool, version, query, retrieval time, award identifier, and URL.
search_strategy: Use only in an approved environment. A mapped award remains evidence, not a ranking or suitability finding.

name: GSA CALC+ via 1102tools
purpose: Research federal awarded labor ceiling rates.
limitations: Ceiling rates are not actual rates paid or fully burdened cost estimates.
method: Match labor categories, contract conditions, and geographic assumptions.
use_when: Optional: use for ceiling labor-rate context through an approved 1102tools MCP host.
questions: What ceiling rates apply to a labor category?
authentication: Requires an approved MCP host; some sources may require access.
record_how: Record the labor category, schedule/contract, date, source, and limitation. Ceiling rates are not paid rates.
search_strategy: Use only in an approved environment and preserve the upstream source and date.

name: BLS OEWS via 1102tools
purpose: Find occupational wage benchmarks.
limitations: Wage statistics are not the same as vendor hourly billing rates.
method: Record occupation, geography, year, and any data suppression caveat.
use_when: Optional: use for occupational wage benchmarks through an approved 1102tools MCP host.
questions: What occupational wage benchmark applies?
authentication: Requires an approved MCP host and network access.
record_how: Record the occupation, geography, period, source, and limitation. A wage benchmark is not a vendor billing rate.
search_strategy: Use only in an approved environment and retain the upstream series or table reference.

name: Acquisition.gov via 1102tools
purpose: Investigate FAR Overhaul language, agency deviations, and source guidance.
limitations: Model language alone does not establish which rule governs a particular procurement.
method: Inspect dates, agency-specific deviations, and operative authority.
use_when: Optional: use for acquisition policy retrieval through an approved 1102tools MCP host.
questions: What does the current FAR or agency policy say?
authentication: Requires an approved MCP host and network access.
record_how: Record the tool, query, part/section, effective date, retrieval time, and URL.
search_strategy: Use only in an approved environment and verify the current text before relying on it.

name: eCFR via 1102tools
purpose: Retrieve CFR provisions, history, and associated clauses.
limitations: An AI summary is not a legal applicability determination.
method: Quote and link to applicable text as-of a particular date.
use_when: Optional: use for regulation retrieval through an approved 1102tools MCP host.
questions: What does the operative regulation say as of a date?
authentication: Requires an approved MCP host and network access.
record_how: Record the title/part/section, as-of date, tool, retrieval time, and URL.
search_strategy: Use only in an approved environment and confirm currentness.

name: CMS gov-codejson and SHARE IT guidance
purpose: Discover agency software inventory metadata and reuse conditions.
limitations: An inventory entry does not prove that software is fit for the user's need.
method: Look for code.json, agency indexes, repository visibility, license, and maintenance.
use_when: Use to find government software metadata and reuse candidates.
questions: Is there government-developed code for this function? What license, version, maintenance, and usage are reported?
record_how: Record the repository URL, metadata source, version/date, license, reported status, and limitations. Listing is not suitability.
search_strategy: Search metadata by function and agency, then inspect the repository and license separately.

name: publiccode.yml
purpose: Discover and describe public-sector software using an established metadata convention.
limitations: Metadata completeness and field semantics vary by project and version.
method: Validate claims against project source code, governance, and documentation.
use_when: Use to read publiccode.yml metadata about a public-sector codebase.
questions: What does the project report about ownership, license, maintenance, and version?
record_how: Record the metadata URL, version/date, license, and limitations. Verify the repository and reuse rights separately.
search_strategy: Find the project metadata, then check the source repository and license.

name: DITAP Core Curriculum
purpose: Guide research questions, responsible industry engagement, and the market research case study.
limitations: Curriculum material is educational, not agency-specific approval authority.
method: Use Module 2 Sprint 4 learning outcomes and the Live Digital Assignment rubric.
use_when: Use for the DITAP market-research method and workshop context.
questions: What does the curriculum expect for this market research activity?
record_how: Record the module or page and date. This project is independent of DITAP.
search_strategy: Read the module guidance and adapt it to agency policy; it is educational, not binding.

name: Digital.gov digital-first public experience guidance
purpose: Examine usability, accessibility, content, mobile, service quality, and the public experience.
limitations: Determine applicability of policy provisions and current agency rules independently.
method: Translate applicable outcomes into verifiable evaluation questions.
use_when: Use to check digital-first public experience guidance.
questions: Does the digital-first guidance apply? What user experience or channel considerations matter?
record_how: Record the guidance page and date and distinguish guidance from a binding requirement.
search_strategy: Read the current guidance and confirm applicability with agency policy.
